featureRef: 23.2 Assigning a user to a branch
name: Give a user access to a branch and record the role they hold there
priorityReason: Nothing else gives a user access to a branch, and the role-on-the-assignment rule is what makes one account work at two campuses.

goal.capability: to assign a user to my branch and record the role they hold here
goal.outcome: the person can work at this campus in the role this campus needs, whatever they are elsewhere

secondaryActors.involvement: Does not assign users to branches. It seeds only the first Principal or School Admin of a new branch.

additional.description: A staff record is created at the branch and needs an assignment to work there.

preconditions.condition: The branch exists and is active.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is the School Admin of that branch (BR-1).

postConditions: The user is assigned to the branch with the role they hold there.
The role belongs to the assignment, not to the user, so a person who is School Admin at one campus and a teacher at another holds two assignments on one account.
The assignment was made by the branch's own School Admin, since staffing a campus is operational work and belongs to the branch.
The Super Admin made no assignment, having been kept out of operational work.
A user holding more than one assignment can move between them.
A withdrawn assignment is kept on the record rather than removed.
Nothing was duplicated. One person is one account, however many branches they work at.

permissions.notes: Assigns users to their own branch and sets the role each holds there (BR-1).
Sees who is assigned to their branch.
Does not assign users to branches, having been kept out of operational work. Seeds only the first Principal or School Admin of a new branch (BR-3).
Sees which branches they are assigned to and in what role.

businessRules.rule: The School Admin of the branch assigns the user to it, recording the role that user holds at that branch. Staffing a campus is operational work and belongs to the branch, not to the Super Admin.
The role belongs to the assignment, not to the user. A person who is School Admin at one campus and a teacher at another is expressed as two assignments carrying two roles on one account.
The Super Admin does not assign users to branches, having been kept out of operational work as elsewhere in the system. It seeds only the first Principal or School Admin of a new branch.
A user holding more than one assignment moves between them by switching branch. They do not sign in twice.
An assignment is withdrawn when the user no longer works at that branch, and the record of it is kept. A person who worked at a campus for two years should still be traceable there.
One person is one account, however many branches they work at. Two accounts for one person produce two attendance records, two payroll entries and two leave balances.

Where a member of staff is to hold a post at a second branch at the same time, that is a multi-branch assignment with its own approval. Where they are moving branches permanently, that is a transfer. Neither is an ordinary assignment made here.
A user cannot hold two active assignments at the same branch. A change of role at a branch replaces the role on the existing assignment.
An assignment is never made to a deactivated branch.
A School Admin cannot assign a user to a branch other than their own, since branches are sealed.

transitions.condition: The user no longer works at that branch. The record is kept (BR-5).
The user returns to the branch.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Assigns to their own branch only, and refuses a deactivated one.

basicFlow.navigation: Assign a user → Select the role at this branch
basicFlow.userAction: Records the role the user holds at this branch.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the role on the assignment rather than on the user.
Adds the assignment to the user's existing account rather than creating a second account for them.
Shows that the user holds an assignment elsewhere, without detail of what they do there.

basicFlow.userAction: Sees which branches they are assigned to and in what role, and moves between them.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Lists the assignments. Switching between them is a separate act.

basicFlow.userAction: Changes the role a user holds at this branch.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Replaces the role on the existing assignment rather than creating a second.

basicFlow.userAction: Withdraws the assignment when the user no longer works at the branch, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Ends the access and keeps the record.

alternateFlows.condition: The user is a School Admin elsewhere and a teacher here
alternateFlows.behaviour: Two assignments carry two roles on one account, since the role belongs to the assignment (BR-2, BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: A user's role at this branch changes
alternateFlows.behaviour: The role on the existing assignment is replaced. A user cannot hold two active assignments at one branch (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The staff member is to hold a post at a second branch at the same time
alternateFlows.behaviour: That is a multi-branch assignment with its own approval by both branches, not an ordinary assignment made here (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The staff member is moving branches permanently
alternateFlows.behaviour: That is a transfer, which keeps the employment continuous, not an assignment and a withdrawal (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: The user returns to the branch later
alternateFlows.behaviour: The withdrawn assignment is reactivated rather than a second created, so the history stays whole (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: The Super Admin attempts to assign a user
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. The Super Admin seeds only the first Principal or School Admin of a new branch (BR-3).

departures.requirement: There is no route that creates a second account for a person who already has one. Two accounts produce two attendance records, two payroll entries and two leave balances.

departures.aspect: The role is on the assignment
departures.requirement: A role is never held by a user globally. It is always held at a branch, so the same person can be a School Admin at one campus and a teacher at another.
No user is assigned to a branch by anybody outside it. The Super Admin seeds only the first administrator of a new branch.
An assignment is never deleted, so a person who worked at a campus stays traceable there.
Assignments are retained 7 years after withdrawal, since attendance, payroll and audit records reference them.

openQuestions.question: Who assigns a user to a branch when that branch's only School Admin has left?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The Super Admin seeds only a new branch, not a stranded one.

openQuestions.question: Can a School Admin assign somebody the School Admin role at their own branch?
openQuestions.assumption: Modelled as possible. It means a School Admin can create a peer.

openQuestions.question: Does withdrawing a user's last assignment disable their account, or leave it with no branch?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. An account with no assignment can do nothing but exists.

openQuestions.question: Is a Principal assigned per branch in the same way, or does a Director sit above branches?
openQuestions.assumption: Per branch as modelled, unless granted a consolidated view.

openQuestions.question: Where a user is assigned at two branches with different roles, which role governs a group-level screen?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified, and only a consolidated view holder would see one.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
